name: Retrieval-augmented NLP

conventions.text: Write the worked example into the figure: real input or passage text set in a typewriter face, with the words that matter (the masked span, the unsupported claim) in red.
Draw the knowledge corpus as a storage glyph (a database cylinder or a clipped-corner document note), not as a module box.
Draw retrieval links as dashed arrows and keep solid arrows for the model's own data flow.
Give each input chunk or retrieved passage an identity mark (its own fill colour, or a numbered disc) and repeat that mark wherever the item is used later.
Show what was selected by highlighting it in place: light up the chosen path and fade the rest, or wrap the winning item in a coloured outline.
Stand in for the language model and the retriever with small icons or glyphs (an LLM logo or network icon, a magnifier, a pair of trapezoids) rather than labelled boxes.
Compare two runs (two training stages, or baseline vs method) as side-by-side copies of the pipeline with no frame around either half; whitespace or a single rule separates them.

Draw text as rows of small equal rounded token cells, one fill per source (query vs document, input chunk vs context-only), and keep the fills identical in every panel or stage so the reader tracks tokens by colour.

source: summarised from the evidence cards listed under each convention
